items.directive: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
items.text: The vast community of bacteria [[1:housed]] in the human digestive tract has become one of the most active frontiers in biology. The mix of species in each person's gut [[2:vary]] from birth onward, shaped by diet, medication, and even the manner of delivery. Recent experiments suggest that signals from this hidden community [[3:reach]] the brain through the nervous system, [[4:influencing]] mood and appetite in ways researchers are only beginning to map. Understanding how such tiny organisms steer human health [[5:requires]] tools from genetics, chemistry, and computer science alike, and laboratories around the world are now racing to build them.
rationales: housed는 The vast community를 뒤에서 꾸미는 과거분사이므로 본동사 has become과 충돌하지 않아 옳습니다.
주어 핵은 단수 The mix이고 of species in each person's gut은 전치사구 미끼이므로 단수 동사 varies로 고쳐야 합니다.

Understanding이 이끄는 동명사구 주어는 단수 덩어리이므로 단수 동사 requires는 옳습니다.

items.directive: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
items.text: Psychologists have long questioned whether people can genuinely divide their attention between demanding tasks. In a series of driving-simulator studies, participants [[1:asked]] to hold a conversation while navigating heavy traffic [[2:were]] far slower to notice sudden hazards. What alarms researchers most is that confidence in one's own multitasking skill [[3:bears]] almost no relation to actual performance. The number of drivers who admit to using a phone behind the wheel [[4:have]] risen steadily, even as evidence of the risks accumulates. Reviewing dozens of such findings, several safety agencies now [[5:recommend]] treating attention as a strictly limited resource rather than a skill to be stretched.
rationales: asked는 participants를 뒤에서 꾸미는 과거분사이므로 본동사로 착각하면 안 되며 어법상 옳습니다.
were의 주어 핵은 복수 participants이고 asked ... traffic은 분사 수식어이므로 복수 동사가 옳습니다.

items.text: Community life in modern cities depends on institutions that few residents ever notice. Public libraries, neighborhood councils, and volunteer fire brigades [[1:operate]] largely out of sight, yet they quietly hold local networks together. Sociologists [[2:observing]] these organizations report a worrying pattern. Each of the groups they studied [[3:were]] struggling to replace aging members, and the burden of unpaid work [[4:falls]] on an ever smaller circle of committed citizens. Because so much of a city's resilience [[5:rests]] on this invisible labor, researchers argue that supporting such groups deserves the same priority as repairing roads or bridges.

items.text: Historians reconstructing the medieval spice trade rely on records that merchants never intended as history. Port taxes, insurance contracts, and the diaries of ship captains [[1:reveal]] routes that official chronicles ignore. A single cargo list [[2:recovered]] from a sunken vessel can overturn assumptions [[3:held]] for generations. The prices recorded in this scattered paperwork [[4:show]] that pepper moved across continents faster than most scholars once believed. Among the most valuable sources [[5:is]] the letters exchanged between trading families, whose casual remarks about storms and pirates preserve details that no official ledger could.

items.text: The debate over how far restorers should go in repairing damaged paintings [[1:have]] divided the art world for more than a century. Some conservators argue that every crack and faded patch [[2:carries]] historical information, and that removing later additions [[3:erases]] part of an object's biography. Others reply that a painting [[4:left]] beneath layers of grime cannot speak to viewers at all. Between these camps, museums have crafted uneasy compromises that [[5:vary]] from gallery to gallery, which is why two canvases by the same master can emerge from restoration looking strikingly different. Advances in imaging technology now allow restorers to preview their choices, yet the deeper question of how much intervention history can bear remains open.
rationales: 주어 핵은 단수 The debate이고 over how far ... paintings는 두 겹 수식어이므로 단수 동사 has로 고쳐야 합니다.

items.text: Coastal wetlands rank among the most productive ecosystems on the planet, yet they continue to disappear at an alarming rate. The grasses [[1:anchoring]] the mud absorb the force of incoming storms, and a single acre of marsh [[2:stores]] more carbon than most forests of comparable size. Nearly half of the wetlands that existed a century ago [[3:has]] already vanished, drained for farmland or buried under expanding ports. What makes the loss so difficult to reverse [[4:is]] the slow pace of natural recovery: once salt water intrudes, replanting programs [[5:take]] decades to restore even a fraction of the original habitat.

items.text: Economists who measure national wealth have long struggled with activity that never appears in official statistics. Street vendors, family workshops, and unregistered repair shops [[1:generate]] a substantial share of income in many developing economies. The value created in these informal sectors [[2:escapes]] taxation, which weakens public budgets even as millions of households depend on it. There [[3:remains]] considerable disagreement about how such work should be counted, since surveys capture only what respondents choose to reveal. Behind the seemingly precise figures of national accounts [[4:lies]] countless judgment calls about what deserves to be included. Reforming the way output is measured [[5:has]] therefore become a quiet priority for international statistical agencies.

items.text: Recommendation systems now shape what billions of people read, watch, and buy. Behind these effortless suggestions [[1:stands]] an elaborate model trained on billions of recorded clicks. Predicting what millions of users will click next [[2:require]] enormous computing power, and the systems [[3:designed]] to gather the necessary data record nearly every action we take online. Critics note that each of these engineering choices [[4:reflects]] commercial priorities rather than the wellbeing of users, and that the habits formed under constant algorithmic guidance [[5:are]] proving difficult to unlearn. As the technology spreads into education and healthcare, questions about who controls it grow harder to ignore.
